best_moment.what: Promoted to Senior Director after disclosing everything in the background check. Being honest and having it actually work was the most satisfying payoff.

worst_moment.what: The GE. I lost the ward at 48.2% and the card said it was never about me anyway. After 24 years of choices it felt like the game shrugged at me.

skip_year.why: The quiet years where I was just resting and losing a bit of REP and COMP were dull, but none were bad enough to want gone. I would have just tapped through them.

answer.held_back_by: My REP was too low because I kept choosing the honest, do-the-work, go-home options over being seen and networking. I think the game rewards visibility for the political route, and I never built it. The election result also seemed partly out of my hands.
answer.ending_fair_why: INTEG was 100 and I got through nearly every test cleanly, but the ending says it was never about me. I get that it is a point about the system, but it felt like a shrug after all that work. I also never really understood what REP and STAND do, so I could not have steered towards a different result.
answer.chase_next: Become an MP or minister. I would network more from early on to get REP up past 60, run in a single seat, and see what the minister path looks like and what the pay is.
answer.play_again_why: I want to see what happens if I go for visibility instead of going home, and a run is quick enough to try it. I'm a bit annoyed about the loss, which helps.
answer.title_fit_why: The game is mostly about surviving appraisals and climbing grades, and I never even reached minister. The title Minister Salary sounds like a joke about pay, but the pay was not what I remember about the run.
